title: The relative Frobenius factorization
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let
$f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, write $f:X\to Y$ for its base change to $k$ [def-pc-base-change], and let
$\Phi_X,\Phi_Y$ be the $q$-power scheme Frobenii of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m\geq1$ put

$$
X'_m=Y\times_{\Phi_Y^m,Y,f}X,
\quad p_m:X'_m\to X,\quad f'_m:X'_m\to Y,
\quad r_m=(f,\Phi_X^m):X\to X'_m,
$$

where the fibre product and its universal pair map are those of
[def-pc-fibre-product], and $f'_m$ and $p_m$ are the first and second projections, so
that $\Phi_Y^mf'_m=fp_m$. The map $r_m$ is defined because
$\Phi_Y^mf=f\Phi_X^m$: with $Q=q^m$, the maps $\Phi^m$ are the base
changes $\Phi_0^m\times\operatorname{id}_k$ of the absolute
$Q$-power Frobenii of the $k_0$-schemes $X_0$, $Y_0$ (their affine
incarnation is $a\mapsto a^Q$), and absolute Frobenius commutes with
every morphism of $\mathbf F_p$-schemes. By construction

$$
p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m,\qquad f'_mr_m=f .
$$

*The relative Frobenius.* Write $F_{X_0},F_{Y_0}$ for the absolute
$Q$-power Frobenii of $X_0,Y_0$
[def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] and put
$X_0^{(Q)}=Y_0\times_{F_{Y_0},Y_0,f_0}X_0$. The *relative
$Q$-power Frobenius* of $X_0$ over $Y_0$ is
$F_{X_0/Y_0}=(f_0,F_{X_0}):X_0\to X_0^{(Q)}$. Since fibre products
commute with the base change $k_0\to k$ and
$\Phi=\Phi_0\times\operatorname{id}_k$,

$$
X'_m=X_0^{(Q)}\times_{k_0}k,\qquad
r_m=F_{X_0/Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k .
$$

Affine-locally, for $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y_0$ and
$\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq f_0^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)$, the
scheme $X_0^{(Q)}$ has the corresponding affine open
[lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]
which is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{F,R}S)$, the
tensor product along $F:R\to R$, $r\mapsto r^Q$, on the left factor,
and $F_{X_0/Y_0}$ is given by

$$
R\otimes_{F,R}S\longrightarrow S,\qquad r'\otimes s\longmapsto
f_0^\#(r')\,s^Q ,
$$

which is well defined because $r'r^Q\otimes s$ and $r'\otimes f_0^\#(r)s$
have the same image $f_0^\#(r')f_0^\#(r)^Qs^Q$.

proof.text: Put $Q=q^m=p^{am}$. On $X_0$ and $Y_0$, the $m$-fold iterates of their $q$-power Frobenii are the absolute $Q$-power Frobenii: on sections, successive powers give $(s^{q^j})^q=s^{q^{j+1}}$, and their underlying maps remain the identity. For every open $V\subseteq Y_0$ the ring homomorphism $f_0^\sharp_V$ satisfies $f_0^\sharp_V(s^Q)=f_0^\sharp_V(s)^Q$. The composition formula for morphisms of locally ringed spaces therefore gives $F_{Y_0}f_0=f_0F_{X_0}$, both on spaces and on every component of the structure-sheaf map. This proves naturality here directly, rather than assuming it from a definition of Frobenius.

source.place: Tag 0CC7, label lemma-frobenius-endomorphism-identity, proof; Tag 0CCG, label remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius, first displayed formula, with n=am

proof.text: For morphisms over $k_0$, base change preserves identity and composition: the base change of a composite and the composite of the induced maps have the same projection to the original scheme and the same projection to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence are equal by fibre-product uniqueness. Starting at the identity and applying this observation to the next composite proves by induction that $\Phi_X^m=F_{X_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$ and $\Phi_Y^m=F_{Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$. Base-changing the equality in step 1 now gives $\Phi_Y^mf=f\Phi_X^m$. The $q$-power model maps are $k_0$-morphisms by the scheme-Frobenius convention; so their iterates and all the base changes just used are morphisms over the stated bases.

source.place: paragraph beginning The map r_m is defined because; base-change functoriality expanded using the universal property of Stacks Tag 01JP

proof.text: Choose $X'_m$ as the fibre product of $\Phi_Y^m:Y\to Y$ and $f:X\to Y$, with first projection $f'_m$ and second projection $p_m$. Its defining equality is $\Phi_Y^mf'_m=fp_m$. By step 2 the pair $(f,\Phi_X^m)$ has equal composites to $Y$, so the fibre-product universal property gives the unique $r_m:X\to X'_m$ with $f'_mr_m=f$ and $p_mr_m=\Phi_X^m$. Applying the same construction over $k_0$, using step 1, defines $X_0^{(Q)}$ and $F_{X_0/Y_0}=(f_0,F_{X_0})$, with its two projection equalities. This is the n-fold relative Frobenius construction of Stacks with n=am, with the two factors written in the opposite order.

source.place: Tag 0CC9, label definition-relative-frobenius; Tag 0CCG, label remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius, defining diagram

proof.text: Here is the base-change identification, including its effect on the arrow. For any scheme $T$, a pair $a:T\to Y$, $b:T\to X$ with $\Phi_Y^ma=fb$ is equivalently a triple $(a_0:T\to Y_0,b_0:T\to X_0,t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$ satisfying $F_{Y_0}a_0=f_0b_0$ and the common $k_0$-structure equalities. Indeed the equation on $Y$ forces the two projections to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to coincide, and its other projection is exactly the displayed model equation. The same triples specify maps to $X_0^{(Q)}\times_{k_0}k$. Applying the universal pair maps in each direction and then projection uniqueness gives inverse scheme morphisms, the canonical isomorphism $X'_m\cong X_0^{(Q)}\times_{k_0}k$. Under it $r_m$ has model components $(f_0\pi_X,F_{X_0}\pi_X)$ and $k$-component the structure map of $X$, exactly the components of $F_{X_0/Y_0}\times_{k_0}\operatorname{id}_k$; hence these arrows agree. The equal signs in the statement denote these projection-compatible canonical identifications.

source.place: paragraph beginning Since fibre products commute with the base change; the universal-property argument supplies the details

proof.text: Take $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y_0$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq f_0^{-1}(U)$, and let $g:R\to S$ be the ring map of $f_0|_V$. The absolute Frobenii restrict to $U$ and $V$, are identity maps on their spaces, and on these affine opens are induced by the $Q$-power ring maps. The open-fibre-product statement identifies $U\times_{F_{Y_0}|_U,U,f_0|_V}V$ with the corresponding open of $X_0^{(Q)}$. The affine-fibre-product statement identifies this open, compatibly with both projections, with $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{F,R}S)$, where the base ring $R$ acts on the left copy of $R$ by $r\mapsto r^Q$ and on $S$ by $g$. The inverse image of that open under $F_{X_0/Y_0}$ is $f_0^{-1}(U)\cap F_{X_0}^{-1}(V)=V$, since $F_{X_0}$ is identity on spaces and $V\subseteq f_0^{-1}(U)$. Thus its affine incarnation is a ring map $R\otimes_{F,R}S\to S$, whose composites with $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$ and $s\mapsto1\otimes s$ are respectively $g$ and $s\mapsto s^Q$.

source.place: Tag 01JR, label lemma-open-fibre-product; Tag 01I4, label lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, formula and proof; the restriction of absolute Frobenius is as in varieties.tex Tag 03SM

proof.text: Apply the tensor-product universal property with the left algebra $R$ having structure map $r\mapsto r^Q$, the right algebra $S$ having structure map $g$, and the target ring $S$ having $R$-algebra structure $r\mapsto g(r)^Q$. The maps from the two factors are $g:R\to S$ and $F_S:S\to S$, $s\mapsto s^Q$. They are ring homomorphisms by the iterated ring-Frobenius statement, and are maps of these $R$-algebras because $g(r^Q)=g(r)^Q=F_S(g(r))$. The cited universal property gives the ring homomorphism $h(r'\otimes s)=g(r')s^Q$, uniquely determined by the two factor maps. By step 5 and functoriality and faithfulness of affine spectra, its spectrum is the restriction of $F_{X_0/Y_0}$. In particular $h(r'r^Q\otimes s)=g(r')g(r)^Qs^Q=h(r'\otimes g(r)s)$, the balancing relation in the statement. This checks the twisting explicitly and requires no flatness, reducedness or perfection of $R$ or $S$.
